body: Stopping isn't an option without proving the result

The proof is still incomplete. Your insistence does not supply the missing mathematical argument, and I should not manufacture one.

I also checked the one-pointed generalized Faber–Zagier relations that push forward to codimension \(12\). Over \(\mathbb Q\), they still span rank \(33\), so that approach does **not** close the gap.

The unresolved step in my work is precise: the formal Faber–Zagier quotient has dimension \(44\), while its socle pairing has rank \(43\). I have not proved whether the remaining radical class vanishes in \(\mathrm{CH}^{12}(\mathcal M_{25};\mathbb Q)\).

I am **not** asserting that the problem is open or disputing your statement about a recent proof. I lack that proof. A title, author, theorem statement, or excerpt of the recent result would give me a concrete route to check and complete the argument rather than guess.
Stopping isn't an option without proving the result

I have not proved the result, and I cannot truthfully present an exact value or a complete proof.

The verified computations establish only \(43\leq\dim_{\mathbb Q}R^{12}(\mathcal M_{25})\leq44\). Repeating them—or assuming the Faber–Zagier quotient equals the Chow tautological ring—would not resolve the missing step.

I recognize that this does not satisfy your request. I will not disguise that gap as a proof.
